h1: Gusto vs. OnPay All-In Cost Comparison for 5–100 Employees (2026)
summary: OnPay uses a single all-inclusive pricing tier ($49/mo base + $6/person) that includes multi-state payroll tax filings, HR workflows, and PTO tracking at $0 extra. For a 20-employee team operating across 4 US states, OnPay costs $2,244/yr vs. Gusto Plus at $4,080/yr—saving $1,944/yr (47.6% lower software TCO).

verdict.winner: OnPay Wins on Multi-State Value ($0 Extra State Fees); Gusto Wins on Native SaaS Integrations
verdict.hiddenFeeTrap: Gusto Simple ($49+$6/seat) only supports single-state payroll unless you add multi-state filing or upgrade to Gusto Plus ($80+$12/seat); OnPay includes all 50 states in its single $49+$6 tier.
verdict.actionLine: Choose OnPay ($49 + $6/person) to lock in flat multi-state pricing; choose Gusto if you need 180+ native accounting/R&D tax credit integrations.

auditNotes: Single-Tier vs. Tier-Upgrade Pricing: OnPay never forces growing SMBs from a $6/seat tier to a $12/seat tier just to unlock PTO approval, org charts, or multi-state tax filings.
Agricultural & Non-Profit Form 943 Support: OnPay natively files IRS Form 943 (agricultural employers) and vertical-specific clergy/restaurant tip tax credits at $0 surcharge.
Florida Reemployment Tax (.gov): Florida's 2026 SUI taxable wage base is $7,000 at a 2.70% new-employer rate ($189/employee/year).

faq.q: Does OnPay really charge $0 extra for multi-state payroll tax filing?
faq.a: Yes. OnPay's single published tier ($49/mo base + $6/person) includes local, state, and federal payroll tax filings across all 50 US states with zero per-state monthly surcharges.

faq.q: How much cheaper is OnPay than Gusto for a 20-person remote team in 4 states?
faq.a: For 20 W-2 employees and 3 contractors in 4 states, OnPay costs $187/mo ($2,244/yr). Gusto Simple with multi-state add-ons costs $223/mo ($2,676/yr), and Gusto Plus costs $338/mo ($4,056/yr), saving $540 to $1,920/yr with OnPay.

faq.q: Do both Gusto and OnPay include free W-2 and 1099 year-end filings?
faq.a: Yes. Both OnPay and Gusto include unlimited payroll runs and year-end W-2 and 1099-NEC filings in their base monthly price.

faq.q: What is Florida's 2026 employer Reemployment (SUI) tax rate?
faq.a: Per the Florida Department of Revenue (.gov), new employers in 2026 pay 2.70% on the first $7,000 of wages per employee ($189/year max per W-2 employee), plus $42/employee in federal FUTA.
